limitations.statement: The model currently uses four types of prior knowledge; other essential information such as enhancers and protein sequences could potentially improve performance.
Only transcriptional data at single-cell level were used; integration of epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data is a future direction.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.
In silico perturbation predictions require experimental validation, as demonstrated for gonadal differentiation candidate genes.
GeneCompass only incorporates data from two species: human and mouse. Inclusion of other species may be offset by species-specific expression patterns.
Homologous genes not available for all genes; species-specific Ensembl IDs were used for non-homologous genes.

methods.description: 12-layer transformer (L=12, H=12, D=768) with GELU activation, dropout 0.02, layer-norm epsilon 1e-12. Pre-trained with batch size 10, learning rate linear decay with 10,000 warm-up steps, max lr 5e-5, AdamW optimizer, for 3 epochs on 4x8 NVIDIA A800 GPUs. Input: top 2048 genes per cell after ranking by expression, concatenated absolute expression value and gene ID, plus species token. Four prior knowledge types (promoter, GRN, gene family, co-expression) encoded into unified embedding space. Masked language modeling: 15% of genes masked; multi-task loss: L = (1-β)L_ID + βL_exp (β hyperparameter).
